<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|192|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XVIII.}}</noinclude>consummate vvhich vvere vvritten by the Prophets of the sonne of man. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=32}}† For he shal be deliuered to the Gentiles, and shal be mocked, and scourged, and spit vpon: {{verse|chapter=18|verse=33}}† and after they haue scourged him, they vvil kil him, and the third day he shal rise againe. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=34}}† And they vnderstoode none of these things, and this vvord vvas hid from them, and they vnderstoode not the things that vvere said.

{{verse|chapter=18|verse=35}}† And it came to passe, vvhen he drevv nigh to Iericho, a certaine blinde man sate by the vvay, begging. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=36}}† And vvhen he heard the multitude passing by, he asked what this should be. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=37}}† And they told him that {{sc|Iesvs}} of Nazareth passed by. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=38}}† And he cried saying, {{sc|Iesvs}} sonne of Dauid, haue mercie vpon me. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=39}}† And they that vvent before, rebuked him, that he should hold his peace. But he cried much more, Sonne of Dauid haue mercie vpon me. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=40}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} standing, commaunded him to be brought vnto him. And vvhen he vvas come neere, he asked him, {{verse|chapter=18|verse=41}}† saying, VVhat vvilt thou that I doe to thee? but he said, Lord, that I may see. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=42}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to him, Do thou see, thy faith hath made thee vvhole. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=43}}† And forthvvith he savv, and folovved him, magnifying God. And al the people as they savv it, gaue praise to God.⊣

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XVIII.}}}}

''8. Shal he finde faith.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Church erreth not in faith.}}The Luciferians and Donatists vsed this place to excuse their fall from the Church, as our Aduersaries novv doe, saying that it vvas decaied in faith, vvhen they forsooke it. To whom vve answer as S. Hierom {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Hier. cont. Lucif. c. 6.''}}and S. Augustin {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Aug. de vnit. Ec. c. 15. & de verb. Do. Ser. 36.''}}answered them, that Christ saith not that there should be no faith leaft in earth: but by this maner of speache insinuateth, that at the later day in the great persecution of Antichrist faith should be more rare, and the faithful among so many wicked not so notorious: specially that perfect faith containing deuotion, trust, and affection toward God, which our Maister so praised in certaine vpon whom he wrought miracles, and by force vvhereof mountaines might be moued, vvhich is rare euen vvhen the Church florisheth most.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XIX.}}}}}}

{{c|''In Iericho he lodgeth in the house of Zachæus a Publicane, and against the murmuring Iewes openeth the reasons of his so doing. 11. He sheweth, that the last day should not be yet, 15. and what then in the iudgement he vvil doe both to vs of his Church as wel good as bad, 47. and also to the reprobate Ievves. 29. Being now come to the place of his Passion, he entreth (vveeping and foretelling the destruction of blinde Hierusalem) with triumph as their Christ 45. He sheweth his zeale for the house of God, and teacheth therein euery day. 47. The rulers would destroy him, but for feare of the people.''}}<noinclude>{{rh|||AND}}</noinclude>
